basics.description: **Note:** Please refer to the following before installing the solution: • Review the solution [Release Notes](https://github.com/Azure/Azure-Sentinel/tree/master/Solutions/SonicWall%20Cloud%20Secure%20Edge/ReleaseNotes.md) • There may be [known issues](https://aka.ms/sentinelsolutionsknownissues) pertaining to this Solution, please refer to them before installing. The [SonicWall Cloud Secure Edge](https://www.sonicwall.com/products/cloud-secure-edge) (CSE) solution ingests CSE events into Microsoft Sentinel through the CSE events API, and includes a parser, a workbook, analytic rules, and hunting queries for CSE sign-ins, private access, device trust, and Internet Access. **Underlying Microsoft Technologies used:** This solution takes a dependency on the following technologies, and some of these dependencies either may be in [Preview](https://azure.microsoft.com/support/legal/preview-supplemental-terms/) state or might result in additional ingestion or operational costs: a. [Codeless Connector Framework](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/sentinel/create-codeless-connector) b. [Azure Monitor Logs Ingestion API](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/logs/logs-ingestion-api-overview) **Data Connectors:** 1, **Parsers:** 1, **Workbooks:** 1, **Analytic Rules:** 7, **Hunting Queries:** 6 [Learn more about Microsoft Sentinel](https://aka.ms/azuresentinel) | [Learn more about Solutions](https://aka.ms/azuresentinelsolutionsdoc)

After installing the solution, configure and enable this data connector by following guidance in Manage solution view.

options.text: This solution installs workbook(s) to help you gain insights into the telemetry collected in Microsoft Sentinel. After installing the solution, start using the workbook in Manage solution view.
Gain insights into SonicWall Cloud Secure Edge events: ingestion and connector health, sign-ins and private access, device trust, and Internet Access blocks.
This solution installs the following analytic rule templates. After installing the solution, create and enable analytic rules in Manage solution view.

elements.name: analytic1
elements.label: SonicWall CSE - Event connector failing to fetch data

options.text:
The SonicWall Cloud Secure Edge (CSE) event connector reported a failed data fetch, for
example HTTP 401 after the API key was deleted or expired. While it fails, no CSE events are
ingested, and events from the failure period are not fetched later: after fixing the cause,
disconnect and connect the connector, then backfill the gap.
The rule matches both health records the poller writes: a "Data fetch status change" with
Status Failure (written once, when the status changes) and the hourly "Data fetch failure
summary" (written while failures continue). A poller that stops polling without failing
writes neither; the rule "SonicWall CSE - No events ingested" covers that case.

elements.name: analytic2
elements.label: SonicWall CSE - Device trust level dropped to AlwaysDeny

options.text:
A device's SonicWall Cloud Secure Edge (CSE) trust level changed to AlwaysDeny, so the device
is denied access to protected resources. Causes include failed trust factors (for example
disk encryption or firewall turned off), no trust profile matching the device ("Default"),
or an administrator ban. Alerts once per change: the trust state repeats on every Service
Tunnel event, so only TrustScoring events are evaluated, and an evaluation that stays at
AlwaysDeny does not alert again.
Evaluates events by when they reached Sentinel, so events that arrive late (connector
delay or a backfill) are evaluated once, when they arrive. The query period is 2 days to
include backfilled events, which keep their own time for up to 48 hours.

elements.name: analytic3
elements.label: SonicWall CSE - Failed Command Center admin login

options.text:
A sign-in to the SonicWall Cloud Secure Edge (CSE) Command Center failed (AdminLogin Deny).
CSE logs failed admin logins at INFO severity, so alerting on severity misses them. Admin
sign-in normally goes through MySonicWall single sign-on; a failed sign-in with a local
account, such as the built-in provisioning account, deserves review.
Evaluates events by when they reached Sentinel, so events that arrive late (connector
delay or a backfill) are evaluated once, when they arrive. The query period is 2 days to
include backfilled events, which keep their own time for up to 48 hours.

SonicWall Cloud Secure Edge (CSE) Malware Download Protection blocked a file download as
malicious (Malware Denied). The user's device attempted to download a malicious file; check
how the user reached the source and whether other copies were obtained another way.
Logged at INFO severity. Malware events can reach the API up to about 10 minutes after they
occur.
Evaluates events by when they reached Sentinel, so events that arrive late (connector
delay or a backfill) are evaluated once, when they arrive. The query period is 2 days to
include backfilled events, which keep their own time for up to 48 hours.

No SonicWall Cloud Secure Edge (CSE) events have been ingested for longer than the
threshold. It complements the health rule: it does not depend on health monitoring being
enabled, and it also fires when the connector is disconnected or ingestion stops for a reason
the connector does not report (for example the workspace daily cap).
Possible causes: the connector stopped polling or was disconnected, the API key is invalid,
the workspace daily cap was reached, or CSE produced no events. Check the connector, then
compare with the CSE events API before assuming data was lost.
Set QuietThreshold to the longest normal quiet period for the organization; a short threshold
also fires during quiet periods, such as nights or weekends with no CSE activity. Outages
shorter than the threshold are reported by the connector health rule.

elements.name: analytic6
elements.label: SonicWall CSE - Repeated access denials for one user

options.text:
One user was denied by SonicWall Cloud Secure Edge (CSE) repeatedly within an hour: blocked
connections or requests (Access Unauthorized) and refused sign-ins (Identity Deny), for
example a revoked certificate, a trust score that is too low, or roles with no access to the
service. Repeated denials can indicate a compromised or non-compliant device, an account
trying resources it is not entitled to, or a misconfigured policy.
Matches on type and action, not severity. Each event counts once. Denials are counted per hour of event time.
Evaluates events by when they reached Sentinel, so events that arrive late (connector
delay or a backfill) are evaluated once, when they arrive. The query period is 2 days to
include backfilled events, which keep their own time for up to 48 hours.

elements.name: analytic7
elements.label: SonicWall CSE - Sign-in from a new country for a user

options.text:
A user signed in to, or was refused by, SonicWall Cloud Secure Edge (CSE) from a country not
seen for that user in the previous 14 days. This can indicate stolen credentials or a stolen
device, and also normal travel. Users with no earlier sign-ins in the period are skipped, so
new users do not alert; the "New users" hunting query lists them.
Evaluates events by when they reached Sentinel, so events that arrive late (connector
delay or a backfill) are evaluated once, when they arrive. Country is from the CSE sign-in
event (Identity events); the query period of 14 days is the history compared against.
This solution installs the following hunting queries. After installing the solution, run these hunting queries to hunt for threats in Manage solution view.

This query searches for devices registered with SonicWall Cloud Secure Edge (CSE), with the user, platform, and ownership of each device. This hunting query depends on SonicWallCSEEvents data connector (CSEEvents_CL Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery2
elements.label: SonicWall CSE - Internet Access blocks per user

options.text: This query searches for users with the most SonicWall Cloud Secure Edge (CSE) Internet Access blocks, with the blocked domains, categories, and reasons. This hunting query depends on SonicWallCSEEvents data connector (CSEEvents_CL Parser or Table)

Identifies users whose first SonicWall Cloud Secure Edge (CSE) event in the last 14 days was within the last day, with their devices and locations. This hunting query depends on SonicWallCSEEvents data connector (CSEEvents_CL Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery4
elements.label: SonicWall CSE - Private services accessed per user

options.text: This query searches for the SonicWall Cloud Secure Edge (CSE) private services each user connected to or was denied, with devices and connection counts. This hunting query depends on SonicWallCSEEvents data connector (CSEEvents_CL Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery5
elements.label: SonicWall CSE - Sign-in locations per user

options.text: This query searches for the countries and cities each user signed in from through SonicWall Cloud Secure Edge (CSE), with granted and denied counts. This hunting query depends on SonicWallCSEEvents data connector (CSEEvents_CL Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery6
elements.label: SonicWall CSE - Top sources of denials

options.text: This query searches for client IP addresses and locations with the most SonicWall Cloud Secure Edge (CSE) access denials and refused sign-ins, and the users involved. This hunting query depends on SonicWallCSEEvents data connector (CSEEvents_CL Parser or Table)
